label: conj:modular-s-transform-q-q-tilde
title: Modular $S$-transform $q \leftrightarrow \tilde q = \exp(2\pi i / \tau)$ for Hecke parameter analytic continuation
html:
The framework's H_n(q) Hecke algebra carries a small-q \leftrightarrow root-of-unity duality, and the conjecture below supplies its modular mechanism.

Conjecture (modular S-transform closure). Writing the Hecke parameter as q = e^{2\pi i \tau} for a complex parameter \tau \in \mathbb{H} in the upper half-plane, the modular S-transform \tau \mapsto -1/\tau induces the analytic continuation

  q  \;\longmapsto\;  \tilde q \;:=\; \exp\!\bigl(2\pi i / \tau\bigr).

The substrate enters this picture through its bar image q_0^{-1}, not through q_0. Modular convergence requires \mathrm{Im}\tau > 0. Because q_0 \approx 1.11 > 1, the value q_0 = e^{2\pi i\tau_0} has \mathrm{Im}\tau_0 < 0. Only q_0^{-1} \approx 0.901 < 1 lands in \mathbb{H}. The modular sector is intrinsically bar-symmetric.

The S-transform provides a structural duality. The parameter q admits a bar-symmetric real parameterisation (q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}) and a modular parameterisation (q = e^{2\pi i \tau}). The analytic continuation of every Hecke quantity to the modular parameter is well-defined. The S-transform \tau \mapsto -1/\tau provides a categorical duality complementing the bar involution.

The structural duality

The Hecke parameter has two natural parameterisations:

Parameterisation Relation
Bar-symmetric q (real, framework standard) q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}, bar: q \mapsto q^{-1}
Modular τ (complex, upper half-plane) q = e^{2\pi i \tau}, S: \tau \mapsto -1/\tau

These are distinct parameterisations of the same Hecke algebra. Bar is an involution on the "real" axis of the q-plane; S is an involution on the modular parameter \tau.

The conjecture: the analytic continuation of every Hecke quantity to modular parameter is well-defined, and the S-transform \tau \mapsto -1/\tau gives a categorical duality complementing bar.

Connection to TQFT / Volume Conjecture

The Kashaev Volume Conjecture (conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture) asymptotics are governed by the limit q \to e^{2\pi i / k} as k \to \infty. The S-transform realises this limit as the modular image of the substrate: writing the bar image q_0^{-1} = e^{2\pi i \tau_0} with \tau_0 \approx +0.0166\,i (small positive imaginary, near the cusp \tau \to 0), the S-transform sends \tau_0 \mapsto -1/\tau_0 \approx +60.2\,i — large positive imaginary part, i.e. nome \tilde q \to 0, the root-of-unity / TQFT limit. (The choice of q_0^{-1} over q_0 is the bar-image point of the conjecture statement above; witness computations/probes/d14-theta-bar-side.witness.json.)

This gives the framework an explicit categorical handle on the small-q_0 \leftrightarrow root-of-unity duality.

Relationship to the complex-q lift

The complex-q extension (prop:q-zero-complex-extension

  • prop:lusztig-vs-hermitian-bar) extends the framework's substrate to complex q with |q| > 1. The modular S-transform of this conjecture is the natural continuation of bar beyond the real axis:
  • The bar involution and the Hermitian * coincide on the real axis (q \in \mathbb{R}); they split for \mathrm{Im}(q) \neq 0.
  • The modular S-transform (this conjecture) extends the duality structure to the modular upper half-plane by treating q = e^{2\pi i \tau} as the natural parameterisation.

Together the bar involution, the Hermitian * and the modular S-transform give the framework three distinct \mathbb{Z}/2 involutions on the Hecke parameter, each acting on a different parameter manifold:

Involution Parameter manifold Action
bar real positive axis q \mapsto q^{-1}
Hermitian * complex with \|q\| > 1 q \mapsto \bar q^{-1}
modular S modular \tau \in \mathbb{H} \tau \mapsto -1/\tau

Structural position

  • GB filtration level. None: the S-transform is at the parameter level, not the Hecke-element level.
  • Jet order. All orders: the modular action acts on the entire q-expansion of every quantity.
  • Bar-symmetry. Distinct from bar. The S-transform composed with bar gives a \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2 structure on the modular q-parameter space.

Open R&D

  1. Analytic continuation framework: verify every framework quantity (Hecke generators, Frobenius pairing, Markov trace, Wedderburn weights y_\lambda) has well-defined modular continuation to complex \tau.
  2. Numerical check: at the bar image q_0^{-1} (the convergent branch), compute the S-transform \tilde q_0 and verify the Volume Conjecture asymptotic on \tilde q_0 matches the framework's bare-volume evaluation.
  3. Do not conflate with the named elliptic curves. The modular \tau here is not the period \tau of the Descartes/color curve \mathcal{E}_q (prop:descartes-elliptic-curve): the modular nome is q_0^{-1} \approx 0.90 (near the cusp) while \mathcal{E}_q's period nome is \approx 0.0029 (deep in the fundamental domain) — a \sim\!312\times mismatch.
  4. Connect to the Bloch-group route: the modular S-transform on the K_3(\mathbb{C}) regulator gives a natural framework-side handle on the analytic structure of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm.
  5. Closing the conjecture requires a numerical witness verifying the volume-conjecture asymptotic on \tilde q_0.

Cross-references

  • The complex-q lift: blocks prop:q-zero-complex-extension + prop:lusztig-vs-hermitian-bar
  • Volume Conjecture: conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture
  • The Bloch-group route: conj:borromean-bloch-group-element

Archimedean specialisation. Modular convergence is an archimedean statement: the estimates use \mathrm{Im}\,\tau and \exp over \mathbb{R}, so it sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall.
